newsitem.title: UK: Thatcher's archive to go to Churchill College.
newsitem.headline: Thatcher's archive to go to Churchill College.

text.p: Former British prime minister Margaret Thatcher said on Tuesday that her personal archive would be stored at a Cambridge college named after her hero, wartime leader Sir Winston Churchill.

Thatcher said in a statement that more than 1,000 boxes of her political and personal papers, as well as a large collection of photographs and videos, would be donated to a new charity which would then lend them to Churchill College, Cambridge.
"I have always wanted my papers to stay in the United Kingdom," said Thatcher, the country's longest-serving prime minister this century.

"I am therefore delighted that they are going to Churchill College where they will join the papers of many distinguished 20th century figures, including of course those of Sir Winston Churchill himself."

Thatcher was widely seen as the country's most pugnacious prime minister since Churchill, who led Britain to victory in World War Two, firmly opposed the spread of Communism and stressed the need for Anglo-American cooperation.
Dr Piers Brandon, keeper of the college's archives centre, said he warmly welcomed the news.

"This is without doubt the most important archive of our times, following that of Sir Winston himself. The arrival in Cambridge of the Thatcher papers will mark a formidable gain for scholars of our era," he said in a statement.

Thatcher served as prime minister from 1979 to 1990, winning three consecutive elections for the ruling Conservatives. Senior colleagues forced her to resign in 1990 in an internal party battle over European policy.
Her successor John Major, who was returned to power in 1992, announced on Monday that the next general election would be held on May 1.
